# Implementation Plan: LAN Monitor Dashboard

**Branch**: `[001-lan-monitor-dashboard]` | **Date**: 2026-02-11 | **Spec**: [specs/001-lan-monitor-dashboard/spec.md](spec.md)
**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/001-lan-monitor-dashboard/spec.md`

**Note**: This plan was generated by the `/speckit.plan` command.

## Summary

Build a dashboard to monitor LAN systems (primarily Windows, including legacy) via SSH and HTTP. The system will query system time, disk space (via WMIC), custom command statuses, and software server health via HTTP GET requests. Results will be rolled up into a visual dashboard with "Refresh All" capabilities. The technical approach uses Python 3.11, FastAPI for the web layer, and Paramiko for SSH communication, ensuring compatibility with older Windows environments by using legacy-friendly commands.

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: Python 3.11.x  
**Primary Dependencies**: FastAPI, Paramiko, Jinja2, Uvicorn  
**Storage**: In-memory state store (latest results only)  
**Testing**: Pytest (unit and integration with SSH mocks)  
**Target Platform**: Windows LAN (monitored systems), Linux/Windows (hosting dashboard)  
**Project Type**: Single project (Web Server + Monitor Service)  
**Performance Goals**: Support ~5 systems, dashboard load < 500ms, refresh all < 60s  
**Constraints**: No persistence (restarts clear state), legacy Windows compatibility (WMIC)  
**Scale/Scope**: Small scale (5-10 systems), internal tool  

## Constitution Check

*GATE: Must pass before Phase 0 research. Re-check after Phase 1 design.*

1. **Ship a Working Dashboard**: Plan includes `/health` and `/api/status` endpoints plus HTML dashboard. (PASS)
2. **Secure by Default**: Redacting passwords in logs, localhost binding by default. (PASS)
3. **Reliable & Correct**: Outbound SSH calls will have timeouts; graceful handling of unreachable hosts. (PASS)
4. **Observability**: Structured logging (timestamp, level, message) included in design. (PASS)
5. **Compatibility & Simplicity**: Python 3.11 pinned; minimal dependencies (FastAPI, Paramiko). (PASS)
